2193.note: AAN 2/39/0/13/2067 is in fact digitised (12 scans on szukajwarchiwach) and the scans I opened (nos. 4, 6, 9) are handwritten Russian running prose with no number or letter groups, i.e. the deciphered texts of the telegrams, not ciphertext.

seen.where: https://www.szukajwarchiwach.gov.pl/jednostka/-/jednostka/5324621 (AAN, zesp. 39 Komitet Narodowy Polski w Paryzu, sygn. 2/39/0/13/2067; the unit shows 'Skany (12)', microfilm-derived images); scans 1 (title card), 4 (first leaf), 6 and 9 viewed in Chrome on 5 Nov 2026.
seen.extent: 12 scans; the three text leaves viewed show about 10-15 lines each of continuous handwritten Cyrillic on squared paper, one circled folio number (about 205); the unit's own extent is 8 pages.
seen.cipher: Archive title: 'Archiwum poufne. Telegramy szyfrowe otrzymane przez Ambasade Rosyjska w Rzymie o stosunku tymczasowego rzadu rosyjskiego do organizacji polskich.' Seen: the leaves carry flowing Russian prose paragraphs (the decoded telegram texts), with no digit groups or cipher letters on any leaf viewed (scans 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10-12 not opened); so the unit holds plaintext copies of cipher telegrams, not the cipher.

2238.note: Bethlen Miklos to Gyulafi Laszlo, Teremi 13 August 1667 (not 1666 as in the lead and Lang's row), has a printed postscript of 137 numbers in Jankovics's edition, nos. 70 pp. 185-186, with no decipherment printed there and Lang marking it 'feloldatlan'.

seen.where: Jankovics J. (ed.), Bethlen Miklos levelei I-II (RMPE 6, Budapest 1987), vol. 1 no. 70 (printed pp. 185-186; PDF page 187 of https://szovegtar.iti.mta.hu/site/assets/files/24889/rmpe06-bethlen_1657--1716_1987-1.pdf, text layer read 5 Nov 2026), with the editor's note on PDF p. 631 (autograph, OL P 659, 29. cs. 740); Lang 2015 repertory row C.BethM.03 on p. 281 of https://real-d.mtak.hu/922/7/dc_758_13_doktori_mu.pdf.
seen.extent: Six lines of numbers, about 137 tokens (values 2 to 53, many repeated), after a short clear Hungarian letter dated 'Teremi 13 Augusto 1667'; the edition's transcription (OCR text layer, a few misreadings possible), original not seen.
seen.cipher: Printed letter text: clear body saying he sends an 'Includalt Mese' (included fable) and signs 'Teremi 13 Augusto 1667', followed by the six lines of numbers ('53 2 30 23 30 2 42 52 30 23 2 52 43 23 50 12 ...'); the editor's notes on no. 70 give only the shelfmark and a comment on the content, and no plaintext or key for the number block. The date in the lead and in Lang ('1666. 08. 13.') is wrong: the edition heads the letter 'Teremi, 1667. augusztus 13.' Lang: 'magyar homof., szamok; feloldatlan; reszleges, csak a postscriptum' (Hungarian, homophonic numbers, undeciphered, partial, postscript only).

prior_art.edition: Jankovics 1987 prints the numbers without a decipherment (read on 5 Nov 2026); Lang 2015 (open access thesis) lists it as unresolved and notes Bethlen's 23 Aug 1667 complaint (Jankovics no. 71) of trying eight or nine claves on Bocskai's enclosure without success and of an old great clavis he lacked.
prior_art.literature: Hungarian web search found only general studies of Bethlen's letters and the MEK anthology note on number ciphers with changed keys; no study solving this postscript.

vetting.key_check: No key held here; Gyulafi and Bethlen exchanged a clavis ('Clavissal irt') that is not in the edition; Lang records the clear/resolved Bethlen cipher letters of 27 Jul 1666 (C.BethM.01 and 02, resolved in the edition) as a related system, and the repo's Bethlen family key (targets/transylvania1645, Keresdi Bethlen) is a different substitution; none tested here.
vetting.key_held: Related only: the key resolved in the edition for the 27 Jul 1666 Bethlen letters (Jankovics nos. 26-27) and the Bethlen family key from targets/transylvania1645; neither is known to fit this number block and neither was tested.
